text:
sara_support: Hey team, acme-med reported an outage spike — their on‑prem gateway traffic to our API is being routed to eu-central instead of us-west. Customer sees ~220ms extra per request and EU billing. They claim egress should be via a dedicated peering sitting in us-west.

ken_infra: Can you paste the customer-facing IP they expect and one of the request IDs? Also ask them for a short tcpdump/traceroute. This smells like SNAT/hairpin via the peered hub.

mike_onprem: Customer provided expected egress IP 203.0.113.22 and examples: request-id=rid_0a1b2c. They attached a small pcap (uploaded). Quick tcpdump excerpt: 

``
14:12:03.123 IP 10.10.5.12.54321 > 18.197.45.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:12:03.456 IP 34.200.1.8 > 203.0.113.22: ICMP echo reply
``

mike_onprem: pcap shows source IP getting rewritten to 34.200.1.8 (peered hub egress) before leaving to internet. That IP geolocates to EU.

ken_infra: Yup. Likely flow: onprem -> peering -> hub NAT (SNAT to hub EIP in EU) -> internet -> our EU frontends -> backend routing picks eu because src IP is EU EIP. We prefer region by source IP country tags for capacity/fallback.

jess_product: Is there any short mitigation we can offer customer while infra fixes NAT? Maybe accept a region_hint header?

ken_infra: We support an optional header X-Redwood-Region or ?region_hint param for some customers — but it's only honored for dedicated/private with route policy enabled. Need to check if acme-med tenant has that flag.

deploy-bot: [deployment] routing-policy v2 was last changed 3 days ago by ken_infra.

mike_onprem: Repro steps I used on their gateway (share with infra):

``
# run on gateway to show path to our API:
traceroute -n api.redwood.ai
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood.ai -w /tmp/egress.pcap
# show SNAT rules on hub (from peering admin):
sudo iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v | grep MASQUERADE
``

mike_onprem: Peering admin confirmed they have a generic MASQUERADE rule on the hub that rewrites to the hub EIP pool.

ken_infra: Action items: 1) Confirm acme-med has region_hint allowed (jess to check), 2) Work with peering admin to add exception to preserve original source for peered onprem CIDR (or use EIP per-customer), 3) Add short-term route to force egress via us-west NAT for that CIDR.

jess_product: Acme-med is on private tier and has advanced routing flags enabled. We can flip an operator flag to let region_hint be honored. I'll coordinate with support to offer that as stopgap.

mike_onprem: Quick debug output showing current route selection when source==34.200.1.8: our frontends respond with header `x-redwood-region: eu-central-1` and backend logs show cost routing to EU pool.

ken_infra: Proposed fix (infra): on the hub, replace MASQUERADE with SNAT rule mapping customer CIDR -> preserved/assigned EIP in us‑west, or add conntrack exemption so return path doesn't pass through EU NAT. We'll need peering windows; may be disruptive.

sara_support: Customer is P1 (latency + billing concern). They've accepted region_hint as stopgap. Please prioritize the hub NAT exception.

ken_infra: I'll own the NAT exception. Plan: schedule a 10-minute change to add a SNAT rule scoped to 203.0.113.0/24 -> use eip 198.51.100.77 (us-west). Change window in 30m.

mike_onprem: After we added SNAT mapping, quick validation:

``
$ traceroute -n api.redwood.ai
 1 203.0.113.22 ... -> now path exits via 198.51.100.77
curl -sI https://api.redwood.ai -H 'X-Request-ID: rid_0a1b2c' | grep x-redwood-region
x-redwood-region: us-west-2
``

mike_onprem: Customer confirms latency dropped back to normal (~28ms). Billing routed to US as expected.

jess_product: I'll document the mitigation and add a note in the tenant page about region_hint requirement.

sara_support: Great. Please add postmortem notes: root cause = hub-level MASQUERADE SNAT creating EU egress IP; contributing = region selection based on egress IP with no tenant override.

ken_infra: Adding follow-up: longer term we should: 1) add source-preserving peering templates, 2) surface a diagnostic in Console showing effective egress IP and inferred region, 3) make region_hint automatically allowed for private tenants behind peering.

sara_support: Thanks all — closing ticket after confirmed with customer. :white_check_mark:

(ending log)
